- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 10d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at +10% above prior 10d high.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–7% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is trending upward but true outcome shows downward correction, reduce forecast slope by 15–30% in next 10d window.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact to recent auction events; dampen forecast by 5–10% if sentiment is mixed or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.33/1.00 alternation), model fails to capture volatility; use 3-period moving average of sentiment to adjust forecast volatility.
